subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add a single cross-channel display-only group-entry field, and if so should its canonical public name be `label` rather than `name`?
rationale: The field expands the durable user configuration contract across heterogeneous channel entry shapes; maintainers must decide its naming and scope before an implementation can remain coherent and avoid accidental runtime-name semantics.

options.title: Adopt `label` across supported group entries
options.body: Add an optional string `label` only as preserved display metadata, with no effect on group lookup, access control, or provider name matching.

options.title: Use `name` as display metadata
options.body: Adopt an optional string `name`, while documenting that it is operator-maintained metadata rather than the provider’s current group name.

options.title: Keep opaque keys only
options.body: Decline a new public metadata field and retain IDs as the sole in-config group identifier.

recommendation.title: Adopt `label` across supported group entries
recommendation.body: Add an optional string `label` only as preserved display metadata, with no effect on group lookup, access control, or provider name matching.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cross-channel group configuration contract history and the prior issue discussion both point to steipete for the naming and scope decision.
